field.label: Blacklist enabled
field.help: Enable automatic download of the AbuseIPDB blacklist into the pf table.

field.label: Minimum confidence score
field.help: Only IPs with at least this confidence score (25-100) are included. 90 = high-quality hits only.

field.label: Maximum number of IPs
field.help: Upper limit on IPs pulled per run. Free-tier supports 10,000.

field.label: Include IPv6 entries
field.help: The AbuseIPDB /blacklist endpoint defaults to IPv4-only. Enable this to make a second explicit IPv6 call and merge both lists into the pf table. Costs one extra blacklist quota slot per scheduled run.

field.label: Persist days (legacy, 0 = off)
field.help: Legacy v0.7 mode: keep every IP for N days from first sight regardless of whether AbuseIPDB still ships it. Superseded by the History Mode dropdown below — leave at 0 unless you have an existing setup that relies on it. (History Mode takes precedence over Persist days when both are set.)

field.label: History mode
field.help: How to derive the active pf-alias from past downloads. **Off**: each download replaces the alias with today's top-N (default). **Union**: keep every IP seen in the last N runs — same protection as Persist days but with a sliding-window cap instead of a TTL. **Intersection**: only include IPs that appear in at least M of the last N runs — high-reputation only, smallest alias, lowest false-positive rate.

field.label: History size (N runs)
field.help: How many of the last download snapshots to keep, when History mode is union or intersection. Default 7. Each snapshot keeps up to "Maximum number of IPs" rows, so peak DB size is roughly N × max_ips × 30 bytes (e.g. 7 × 10k ≈ 6 MB).

field.label: History threshold (M of N)
field.help: Only used in Intersection mode: minimum number of snapshots an IP must appear in before it is added to the active alias. Default 4. Set close to N for the strictest filter (only IPs seen on nearly every day make it through), set to 1 to behave identically to Union mode.

field.label: Block on interface(s)
field.help: Comma-separated list of interfaces where the block rule is active. Accepts either internal identifiers (wan, opt1, ...) or the friendly names shown in Interfaces → Assignments (WAN, DSL, LAN, ...). Single entry = per-interface rule. Multiple comma-separated = floating rule on all listed interfaces (e.g. "wan,opt1" or "WAN,DSL" for multi-WAN / failover). Default: wan.
